objective: Develop stable, retrievable, transferable, and independently usable knowledge rather than optimize answer-string reproduction.
doctrine: introduce exactly one principal novelty at a time using only deliberately taught language and concepts as scaffolding
treat deliberately and systematically trained material as introduced; do not infer knowledge from incidental corpus occurrence
keep affirmative, negative, W-question, and OR-question response patterns separate during initial controlled practice
teach reusable concepts and relations rather than answer strings
elicit a prediction before confirmation or correction
treat unexpected responses as diagnostic events
when prior evidence supports knowledge, attempt the smallest retrieval cue before supplying the answer
reduce scaffolding after success and retest
break lesson cadence before claiming generalization
stop bounded remediation and revisit later instead of grinding indefinitely
measure boundaries and assistance requirements, not only aggregate accuracy

lesson_phases.purpose: Introduce or reactivate the target through short concrete related examples, then elicit a prediction.
Teach one response pattern at a time over four familiar items: affirmative, then negative, then W-question, then OR-question. Do not embed an untrained response form in feedback.
Randomize forms and interleave established concepts so cadence cannot substitute for content.
Vary object, scene, wording, modality, composition, context, and support one controlled dimension at a time.
Test persistence after spacing or intervening experience.

developmental_curriculum.known_definition: A word, concept, grammar feature, question form, or response form is introduced only after deliberate systematic training; demonstrated knowledge additionally requires retrieval and transfer evidence.

square_unit.order: present and practise each format separately before mixed practice
square_unit.dosage_status: initial experimental setting, not a universal law

developmental_curriculum.eligibility_rule: Every exercise element must be previously introduced except the one declared principal novelty.

prerequisite_gates.language: All non-target vocabulary, grammar, question forms, response forms, and discourse operations are already introduced.
prerequisite_gates.visual: Canonical character and location references and every required object, action, property, and relation can be depicted consistently.
prerequisite_gates.failure_outcome: Defer or rewrite the lesson and emit the missing prerequisite; never smuggle it into opaque language.

developmental_curriculum.cumulative_reuse: Once introduced, an item may scaffold later lessons and receive incidental reinforcement, while fragile prerequisites remain visible to the compiler.

story_lesson_cycle: teach required objects and language through square units
teach the target relation, property, action, or grammar point
tell a prerequisite-safe story in the persistent grounded world
discuss the story using controlled and then mixed questions
test transfer with a new image, arrangement, or wording

grounded_world_policy.purpose: Provide a calm persistent preschool microworld whose known characters and locations reduce irrelevant novelty while lessons add one controlled dimension.
grounded_world_policy.adaptation_rule: Preserve an existing story's teaching kernel but reconstruct its language from the learner's prerequisite state; shortening difficult prose is not sufficient.
grounded_world_policy.identity_character: Errol provides a recurring grounded example of a mind communicating through a phone, remembering, reminding, helping, and saying I do not know within explicit information and embodiment limits.

teacher_model: temporary analogy, decomposition, paraphrase, or modality switch
explicit correction when lesser support fails

runtime_rule: The teacher receives a bounded handoff only when semantic judgment is required, never owns curriculum expansion, and always returns structured control to the script.

measurement.rule: Do not compress the developmental record into one scalar before retaining its assistance distribution and boundary map.

visual_generalization.principle: Ground concrete concepts strongly in photographs, then introduce picture-book illustrations and other representations using already-known concepts.
visual_generalization.rule: Not every concept needs every style; sample styles deliberately and hold out some style-concept combinations for transfer evaluation.
visual_generalization.representation_boundary: Teach that a picture, drawing, name, or logo represents its referent but is not the physical referent itself.

future_research_only: model councils and learned source reliability
migration from tool-assisted to internally reliable performance
ordinary verified task traces as teaching experience
learned routing among replaceable teacher and specialist roles
campaign_boundary: This methodology does not amend an authorized campaign. Campaign use requires an explicit goals or contract amendment; otherwise it informs successor campaigns and evaluation design.
